Stirling, James (1692-1770)

note.p: Schrift auf der Rückseite des Blattes stark verblasst. Nicht gedruckt bei Tweedie

abstract.p: Stirling erneuert den lange unterbrochenen Briefwechsel. Cramer habe ihn über Bernoullis Wohlergehen und Aufenthalt informiert; nach seiner Abreise aus Italien habe ein längerer Aufenthalt in Schottland seine Auslandskorrespondenz verhindert. Er berichtet über die Überprüfung von Newtons Mondtheorie anhand der Beobachtungen Flamsteeds und Halleys sowie über die von ihm hoch eingeschätzten Verbesserungen Machins. Er erläutert dessen gesonderte Behandlung der radialen Bewegung, einen Satz über gleiche Volumina bei zwei Kraftzentren und die geometrischen Hilfskurven, die Machin Equanten nennt. Cramer habe er ein Interpolationstheorem mittels Quadraturen, ein Reihenbeispiel dazu und ein Beispiel zur Summation einer langsam konvergierenden Reihe übermittelt. Sein Buch über Summation und Interpolation sei im Druck. Er bittet um mathematische Neuigkeiten und erklärt, auf Englisch zu schreiben, weil Bernoulli diese Sprache beherrsche; dieser könne in einer anderen Sprache als Hochdeutsch oder Niederländisch antworten.

Stirling renews their long-interrupted correspondence. Cramer has told him of Bernoulli's well-being and whereabouts; after leaving Italy, a prolonged stay in Scotland prevented him from corresponding with friends abroad. He reports on the comparison of Newton's lunar theory with Flamsteed's and Halley's observations and praises Machin's improvements. He explains Machin's separate treatment of radial motion, a theorem concerning equal volumes under forces directed towards two fixed centres, and the geometrical auxiliary curves called equants. He has sent Cramer a theorem on interpolation by quadratures, a series example, and an example of summing a slowly converging series. His book on summation and interpolation is in the press. He requests mathematical news and explains that he writes in English because Bernoulli understands it; Bernoulli may reply in another language except German or Dutch.

listChange.change: Deutsches und englisches Regest aus dem Brieftext erarbeitet; Kommentarvorschläge geprüft und Erläuterungen zur Mondtheorie, zu Machins Equanten und zum angekündigten Reihenwerk ergänzt; Ortsverknüpfung bei Country nach dem Londoner Briefkontext auf England berichtigt. Der transkribierte Wortlaut bleibt unverändert.

div.opener:
To M.r Nicolas Bernoulli.
Dear Sir
div.p:
It is with the greatest pleasure imaginable that I revive so long an interrupted a cor=
respondence, which I found not only agreable but instructing, I am obliged to owr friend M.r Cramer
for many reasons but particularly that he told me you was well &and where you was. Upon my
leaving Italy I retired into a Corner of Scotland to see my friends and staid longer than
I designed, which among other inconveniencies hindred me from corresponding with any of
my friends abroad. But now I have taken the first opportunity to begin, for I make no doubt
but you have now great store of Mathematical Matters quite new to me, and on the other
hand I shalshall be glad if I find that any thing in owr way in this Country shalshall be
agreable to you. M.r Cramer, as he left England but lately, can inform you of most
things of moment which are on the Anvill. But I shalshall let you know of what has
hapned since he left us, and indeed had raised owr expectation to a great height, but
not to such a pitch as the matter deserved.

You must know that S.r Isaac Newton did not know till a few years before his death to
what degree of exactness his Theory gave the place of the Moon. When it was first pub=
lished, there was a good correspondence betwixt Flamsteed and him, and accordingly Flam=
steed told him that his Theory never disagreed above 2′Das Zeichen bezeichnet Bogenminuten, also jeweils ein Sechzigstel eines Grades. Stirling vergleicht hier die berechnete mit der beobachteten Winkelposition des Mondes; ebenso sind die weiter unten genannten acht Minuten zu verstehen. from the place observed, and
it was commonly believed that all the difference was owing to the uncertainty of
observation. Afterwards when there hapned a Difference between these two Gentlemen, M.r
Flamsteed refused to communicate his Observations, and altho S.r Isaac by the Authority
of Q. Anne got an order to seise his papers, yet he gave but litlelittle credit to
them for that very reason, justly apprehending they might have been given desi=
gnedly false. In short Newton never knew how far his Theory differed from the truth
till D.r Halley succeeded Flamsteed, he has got a fine new Quadrant of 8 feet
Radius fixt in the Meridian, and has now had above 7 years observations of the
Moon with it: From whence it appears that Newton’s Theory differs at most 8′, and
the Difference regularly decreases till it comes to nothing, after which it increases again, but never
exceeds the foresaid limits. D.r Halley designed to compleat
the Theory
by Induction after having taken Observations during an entire Revolution of the Apo=
gee, he wants now but a year more, and perhaps may attain his end.

But M.r Machine has attempted the matter from the original cause, I mean the
Theory of Gravity, and indeed I dare say with great success, altho hitherto he has
only published his chief Theorems without Demonstration, he has shewn the
way of applying them,; they are all extraordinary plain and easy in practice, and
his numbers, when they disagree with Newton’s, come nearer the truth. In short he
has made the most difficult Propositions in the third book of Newton’s more
easy to be understood than can be imagined, or rather to speak more truly, he
has invented more general Propositions of his own, which do the business better,
and which he has demonstrated in a most perspicuous manner,; we must wait his
time for his Demonstrations,Der kurze Druck ist John Machins The Laws of the Moon’s Motion according to Gravity, 1729, als Anhang zu Andrew Mottes englischer Übersetzung von Newtons Principia. Er ist von der hier erwarteten ausführlicheren Darstellung zu unterscheiden. Bernoulli prüft die Schrift kritisch in seiner Antwort vom 22. Dezember 1729; Stirling übermittelt dazu am 30. September 1730 eine Antwort Machins. but in the mean time I shalshall give you the principles
and Method which he uses in his great improvements.

First he has a general way of considering the Motion of the Moon to and from
the Center directly, without considering it’sits angular motion. That is what Kepler calls the
Libratory Motion.Gemeint ist hier die Bewegung zum Kraftzentrum hin und von ihm weg, also die Änderung des Abstands; nicht die scheinbare Schwankung, durch die von der Erde aus wechselnde Teile der Mondoberfläche sichtbar werden. Vgl. Machin, The Laws of the Moon’s Motion according to Gravity, Abschnitt über die libratorische Bewegung. On this principle he has computed the Motion of the Apogeum &and Variation
of the Eccentricity most accurately, the first of which was done but indifferently by
Newton, and the second not at all.

His second principle is that if a body be deflected by two forces tending to two fixt points,
it will describe by lines drawn from it to these two fixt points, equal Solids in
equal times. Which is a noble improvement on Kepler’s equal Areas in equal times
in the case of a body being deflected to one fixt point.Stirling stellt dem Flächensatz für ein Kraftzentrum einen Volumensatz für zwei feste Kraftzentren gegenüber. Bernoulli präzisiert in seiner Antwort vom 22. Dezember 1729, dass die gleichen Volumina um die Verbindungslinie der beiden Zentren beschrieben werden, und bestätigt diesen Satz ausdrücklich. And by this he very easily
explains and computes the Variation of Inclination of the Moon’s Orbite.
He has what he calls his Equants which go through the whole, and are as follows.

Let the Moon for instance move from A to B
it’s Angular Motion with respect to any point S,
will be ASB. Let F be any point, draw lines
from it to A &and B: he constructs a figure, whose Sector
CDF is proportional to the Angle ASB. And finds the point C which will make
the figure CD nearest to a Circle. The Angle ASB may be the Anomaly of the Moon,
the Motion of the Node from the Sun, or Apogee from the Sun, or in short any
Angular Motion. The Curve CD he calls an Equant, it is an Ellipsis in most cases
relating to the Motion of the Moon; this method brings to very easy and elegant
Solutions of many Problems.Machins Equant ist hier eine Hilfskurve, deren überstrichene Sektoren den zeitlichen Verlauf einer Winkelbewegung darstellen; der Name bezeichnet nicht bloss einen Punkt gleichförmiger Winkelbewegung. Bernoulli beanstandet Stirlings Formulierung und insbesondere die Wahl des gesuchten Punkts in seiner Antwort vom 22. Dezember 1729. Vgl. Machin, The Laws of the Moon’s Motion according to Gravity, Abschnitt über den Gebrauch des Equanten.

I lately sent M.r Cramer a Theoreme for interpoling by Quadratures, and now I have sent him
an instance of the same by an infinite Series: and also an Example of finding the Sum of
a slow converging Series. The Book I have now in the press consists in Summing and Inter=
poling of Series, after a Method which I believe is new: he will shew you an Instance of each.James Stirling, Methodus differentialis: sive Tractatus de summatione et interpolatione serierum infinitarum, London 1730. Das Werk behandelt Summation und Interpolation, nicht die Differentialrechnung im heutigen Sinn. Mit seinem Brief vom 30. September 1730 kündigt Stirling die Übersendung des nun erschienenen Buches an.

I shall reckon myself very Lucky if what I here have said, may excite you to send me
some mathematical news, for I am perswaded that you cannot but have good Store of
new inventions which I am a stranger to. I flatter myself that I shalshall soon hear from
you, and I shalshall best know then what particular matters you desire most to be informed about.
div.closer:
I am with great respect
Sir
Your most obedient &and
most humble servant
James Stirling

postscript.p:
P. S. I write to you in English because I know
you are Master of it, but you may write
to me in what language is most easy to you
so as it be neither high nor low Dutch.
